# Audience in plumbing — how Profile A shows up here

Profile A (50+ American DIY homeowner) is defined in core `audience-profiles.md`. This file holds the niche-specific layer: mode, lever ranking, dead levers, money and time language, adversaries, the real mechanisms that keep big titles honest, and safety boundaries.

## 1. The viewer, in this niche

Owns (or recently owned) an older home, often on a fixed or careful income, distrusts being upsold, remembers when things were built to last, takes pride in self-reliance and in protecting the household. Watches faceless how-to / hacks content heavily — the audience tab shows pest control, cleaning, lawn care, home energy and appliances: the same homeowner defending the same castle against different invaders. The September 2026 audience tab added collab-credited face personas (a frugal-living granny, a "Mexican Way" home-hacks network, an HVAC presenter, a nutrition channel, a mechanic) — same castle, more invaders; formats and words transfer from them, topics do not. In one June 2026 week, 7 of the 15 videos this audience watched were plumbing or fixture content on *other* channels — they binge plumbing elsewhere.

**Mode:** browse. They are not typing "how to fix a running toilet" — they are being offered a fear, a saving, or a secret in the feed.

## 2. Lever ranking (best titles pull two or more)

1. **Money protection** — THOUSANDS saved, FREE fixes, micro-cost tricks, exact savings figures. The most-used lever in the channel's own winners.
2. **Fear of home damage** — floods, bursts, FATAL, DISASTER, time bombs, "before they flood your home". Water damage is this niche's apex fear.
3. **Distrust of trades and industries** — the plumber hiding the cheap fix, Roto-Rooter's repeat-customer economics, builder-grade deception, big-box downgrading, "the industry buried this". The persona is the honest insider exception.
4. **Disgust** — gunk, grease, slime, rotting, sewage. Plumbing's unfair advantage; pairs with F20 causal horror.
5. **Pride / competence** — I BET, Most People Get This Wrong, smarter than the plumber's invoice. Confrontational (F6) and sympathetic (F14) both work.
6. **Lost wisdom / nostalgia** — grandpa's tricks, old plumbers, before chemical cleaners existed, built to last. Run honestly through the veteran persona.
7. **Provider / protector identity** — your family, save your home, before vacation, emergency preparedness (F31).
8. **Certainty and permanence** — GUARANTEED removes the fear of wasted effort; FOREVER / PERMANENT ends the recurring chore.
9. **Ease** — ridiculously easy, in minutes, no-scrub, no tools. The friendly trigger for jobs perceived as hard.
10. **Quality-decline narrative** — "they don't make them like they used to" plus the insider workaround (commercial grade, supply house). Deeply resonant.
11. **Urgency** — Tonight, RIGHT NOW, this weekend; do-it-now framing on tiny tasks.

## 3. Dead or weak levers here

- Plain explainers ("S-Traps EXPLAINED In 10 Minutes") sit in the channel's lower tier — every explainer topic wants the banned / REAL-reason re-attack (F21).
- Generic "N uses" breadth (F25 without a fixture) is fatigued in the ecosystem; substance × specific fixture is the live expression.
- F26 "never throw away X" is vocabulary here, not a target.
- Explicit demographic tags ("Safe for Seniors") — candidate only; can read as patronizing.

## 4. Money and time language

- **Scale ladder (one per title):** FREE (terminal — beats "cheap" for this audience) → 50¢ / $1 / $2 / $3 / $5 micro-cost (makes the trick concrete) → "Save $400"-style exact figures (credibility sweet spot) → THOUSANDS (vague-big stakes).
- **Present-progressive loss:** "That ARE Costing You", "Is Already FAILING", "Quietly Costing You" — money bleeding now, not hypothetically.
- **Time:** Tonight, in 10 Minutes, in 60 Seconds, a 5-Minute Test — tiny time makes the mystery credible (F18).
- **Briefs always carry real dollar anchors:** service-call costs, part prices, replacement costs, what the plumber charges for the thing the video does for $6.

## 5. Adversaries

Plumbers as a trade (the persona is the exception), Roto-Rooter, the water company, big-box stores, builders ("builder grade"), brand manufacturers, "the industry". Adversary parentheticals: "(Plumbers Never Mention It)", "(Dealers Hate This)"-style.

## 6. Real mechanisms that support big titles (the honest floor under exaggeration)

The anode rod; the dye-tablet test; rim-jet mineral blockage; wipes and fatbergs (a genuine municipal scandal); big-box SKU downgrading vs supply-house internals (documented fact); free lifetime faucet-cartridge warranties; silent flapper leaks (up to ~200 gal/day); washer hoses as the #1 flood cause; the vinegar + baking-soda volcano as mostly theater; sediment and the rotten-egg smell in water heaters; polybutylene, saddle valves, galvanized, lead solder and Orangeburg as real code stories. Added 2026-09-07: citric acid dissolves calcium carbonate several times faster than vinegar (the honest floor under "it's NOT vinegar" — the Vintage 148k substance itself is TBC); a thermostatic mixing valve lets a tank store at 140°F and deliver at 120°F, roughly 30% more usable hot water, legionella killed in storage, scald risk removed at the tap; in-tank chlorine tablets warp flappers and corrode fill valves and void warranties (Kohler, American Standard, Fluidmaster); oxalic or citric acid lifts iron stains that bleach sets darker; washing soda (sodium carbonate) saponifies drain grease where baking soda only fizzes; a full flush needs the lever held until the tank empties (the exact How To Home tip is TBC). Galvanized pipe is still listed in the model codes — "no longer allowed" is a fake ban; "no plumber installs it anymore" is the honest F21 form. Added 2026-09-07 (Werner briefs): vinegar essence at 25% acetic acid dissolves limescale and urine scale five times faster than 5% vinegar and must never meet chlorine bleach (chlorine gas) or peroxide (peracetic acid); dish soap plus hot, not boiling, water clears most toilet clogs by lubricating the trapway and softening the mass, and boiling water cracks porcelain and softens wax rings; a shower's P-trap is sealed in the floor, so the strainer insert is the whole prevention game; in hard water the running toilet's usual cause is scale on the flush-valve seat; German per-capita water use is roughly 125–130 L/day against ~310 L in the US; the full German-practice list (norms, installation, rituals) is the truth doctrine in `steering.md` §4.

## 7. Safety boundaries (flag inside briefs where relevant)

Gas lines are never DIY push-fit territory. Never mix cleaning chemicals — bleach + ammonia; peroxide + vinegar in-pipe. Boiling-water cautions on porcelain and PVC. Wet-rated vacs only around water. Ice-melt-era emergency content stays inside safe practice.

## 8. Persona-claim discipline (face/persona dial — core `rules-and-specs.md` §2.2)

Roger's "45 years" is a standing claim, fine in voiceover; never attach first-hand dates, named employers, named towns or invented documents to it. Sibling channels keep their own persona bibles — The Vintage Pipefitter has run "45 years" since June 2026 and keeps it; Mark Silverbridge runs a fixed "40 years" (operator, 2026-10-21); Werner Finkbeiner (face) runs the placeholder "30 years" in one greenlit title and needs his number locked before production, plus the face-dial rules in `steering.md` §4 (hedged community claims, no invented German rules, one German word per title). The cautionary example from the audience tab: Frugal Frannie's tenure drifted from 40 years ("25 ILLEGAL Water Bill Tricks…") to 50 ("25 ILLEGAL Laundry Tricks…") across two titles — a persona's number must be constant.
